attempted_axis: Derive the meaning of gGameMode's family bits (0x8000 / 0x4000) from the e_mode enum values, and -- only if the partition reads cleanly -- name them as MODE_GROUP_* masks in include/game/gamemode.h and convert all 20 raw mask sites byte-identically. These sites were deliberately left raw by waves 1-3 (claim.gamemode-raw-site-inventory.20260831.v2) because no single mode constant is a truthful spelling of a family test.

attributes.law_screen: claim.law.raw-offset-form-supplies-value-identity-not-addressing-shape.20260831.v1: APPLIED and decisive, in a STRONGER form than wave 3 used it. Wave 3 respelled literals as enum constants, which is byte-neutral by CONSTANT FOLDING. This pass spells the masks as #define macros expanding to the identical literal token (0x8000 / 0x4000), so the post-preprocessor token stream is character-for-character unchanged and byte-identity holds by CONSTRUCTION, not by a folding argument. That is why macros were chosen over enumerators here (an e_mode enumerator would additionally assert the masks are themselves modes, which they are not). Confirmed: 20/20 sites GATE OK. claim.law.embedded-struct-member-whole-tu-cascade.20260831.v1 and claim.law.aggregate-cascade-tracks-nested-array-not-new-type.20260831.v1: SCREENED, NOT APPLICABLE -- the header addition is two object-like #defines, introducing no type, no aggregate, and no nested aggregate, so the cascade class cannot trigger. Independently confirmed by gating the header edit ALONE across all 19 includers before any consumer edit (19/19 GATE OK), and by adding the include to a 19th, fresh TU (sndfx.c) with no effect. claim.law.lwzu-idiom-web-retention.20260830.v1, claim.law.declared-alias-vs-repeated-cast.20260830.v1, claim.law.multifield-alias-defeats-indexed-addressing.20260830.v2, claim.law.local-alias-vs-direct-global-spelling-diverges.20260831.v1, claim.law.noop-cast-on-array-decay-not-neutral.20260831.v1: SCREENED, NOT APPLICABLE -- no member access, alias, cast node, or address web is created or destroyed by respelling an integer literal as a macro that expands to that same literal; no cast is introduced anywhere in this pass. claim.law.sizeof-defeats-loop-stride-induction.20260831.v1: SCREENED, NOT APPLICABLE but instructive as the near-miss -- it warns that a definitionally-identical substitution (sizeof(T) for a stride literal) can still change codegen because the operand routes through a different front-end path. A macro expanding to the original literal has no such path to route through, which is exactly the distinction that makes this pass safe where the sizeof substitution was not. attributes.scope: DERIVATION VERDICT: CLEAN, with no exceptions. Partitioning all 49 e_mode constants by high bit gives a disjoint three-way split: bit 0x8000 is set on exactly the 11 MA_* ids (MA_CREDITS 0x8000 .. MA_VIEWMENU 0x800A, base ids 0..10); bit 0x4000 on exactly the 13 MG_* ids (MG_PLAYER_SELECT 0x400B .. MG_GWIZ_SPEECH 0x4017, base ids 11..23); NEITHER bit on exactly the 25 bare M_* ids (0..24, including M_CHAR_MANAGEMENT 24, which has no grouped counterpart); and BOTH bits on NO constant. Crucially the two families' base ranges do not overlap either (MA_ covers 0..10, MG_ covers 11..23), so each mask selects one whole family and nothing else, and no bare M_* id can alias into a group (max M_* is 24 = 0x18). Verified verbatim against the Xbox PDB enum e_mode at research/xbox_symbols/misc.h:16779-16830 (the dump is decimal; 32768/16395 etc. convert exactly). NAMES are taken from the enum's OWN prefixes -- MA_ = attract, MG_ = game -- not from an interpretation of behaviour, which is what keeps them honest. All 20 use sites were then read and every one AGREES: gamemain.c:4079 tests the mask inside the attract-loop dispatch itself (the MA_FLYBY switch arm, at a label literally named attract_tail); gamemain.c:3978 lets a start press assign controller 0 during attract; gauntworld.c:6585 writes `(gGameMode & 0x8000) && gGameMode != MA_DEMO && gGameMode != MA_INSTRUCT`, excluding two MA_* ids from the very set the mask selects, which is only coherent if the mask IS the MA_ family; screensaver.c:776 ORs the mask with two specific MG_* ids; items.c:1256 forces the player count to 2 during attract; player.c:716/861/1319 suppress HUD shard/rune display during attract; gamemain.c:1834/4900/4976 skip in-game-only loading. The 0x4000 sites are all in-game-session work (player.c:3257 display setup, gamemain.c:3577 shard checks, gamemain.c:3944 per-player timers, combat.c:2253 camera attention). FILES: include/game/gamemode.h gains `#define MODE_GROUP_ATTRACT 0x8000` and `#define MODE_GROUP_GAME 0x4000` with a full derivation comment. 20 sites converted across 8 TUs: gamemain.c 6 (1280, 1834, 3577, 3944, 3978, 4079, 4900, 4976 -- 8 counting all), player.c 4 (716, 861, 1319, 3257), gauntworld.c 3 (1610, 5059, 6585), items.c 1 (1256), combat.c 1 (2253), message.c 1 (724), screensaver.c 1 (776), sndfx.c 1 (the sndFxPaused() macro at 179). sndfx.c additionally gained `#include "game/gamemode.h"` (it declared its own extern and had no include). 3 commits: 71602ed6f (header), c2c94d1e3 (20 sites), 4403ab9ae (screensaver cap note).
